title: Internal Hom from extension along a stratum
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be an immersion, that is, a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Choose $\tau=\mathrm{et}$ or $\mathrm{proet}$, using the small sites and their size conventions [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. In the pro-etale case assume $X$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, pqf-def-locnoeth]); this includes the finite-type schemes over a field in the enclosing unit. Write $D_\tau(T,A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_\tau,A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix a factorization $S\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$ with $i$ closed and $j$ open. In these ambient categories let $Rs_!=j_!Ri_*$, where $j_!$ is exact extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], and put $Rs^!=Ri^!j^{-1}$, using the ambient right adjoint $Ri^!$ to the closed direct image [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]. Let $Rs_*$ be ordinary derived direct image, computed by a K-injective resolution, and use derived tensor and internal Hom on the ringed sites [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then for all $P\in D_\tau(S,A)$ and $M\in D_\tau(X,A)$ there is an isomorphism
$$
 R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(Rs_!P,M)\ \cong\ Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(P,Rs^!M),
$$
natural contravariantly in $P$ and covariantly in $M$. No boundedness, constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, constructible-preservation, or biduality hypothesis on the complexes is imposed. The assertion applies to either choice of factorization with these properties.

proof.text: For the etale clause, apply Etale.immersionInternalHomIso and discard its additional evaluation normalization. The existing immersionLowerShriek and immersionUpperShriek definitions unfold to the required closed-then-open composites.

For each pro-etale ringed site choose the closed symmetric monoidal structure for the recorded derivedInternalHomOfUniverses and its actual K-flat tensor model. Restrict its representative comparison to flat-term K-flat complexes and apply proEtaleCanonicalTensorComparison. This gives the natural tensor-pullback comparison for the exact intrinsic constant-module pullbacks; no arbitrary alternative tensor is introduced.

Open subschemes of the Noetherian ambient scheme are Noetherian; hence every complementary open immersion used below is quasi-compact. The ringed open-closed theorem and coefficient equivalences give the closed pullback/direct-image counit isomorphism. The closed essential-image theorem gives vanishing after complementary open restriction. Joint zero detection for sheaves implies joint isomorphism detection by applying it to kernels and cokernels. Exact restrictions commute with derived homology, so they jointly detect isomorphisms of unbounded derived complexes, and disjoint-support vanishing also derives.

Transport the fixed-coefficient open extension/restriction adjunction through the actual coefficient equivalences. Identify its right adjoint with the canonical constant-module pullback by uniqueness of adjoints and equality of the canonical direct images. Open extension is fully faithful, so its unit is an isomorphism. Localize the termwise adjunctions of exact functors along quasi-isomorphisms. Their closed counit and open unit remain isomorphisms by localizing the corresponding sheaf isomorphisms. Use the ordinary exact-pullback/right-derived-direct-image adjunction for the composite immersion.

Construct the closed projection map Q tensor Ri_*P -> Ri_*(i^*Q tensor P) as the mate of the tensor-pullback comparison followed by tensoring the closed counit. Its closed restriction is invertible by the counit triangle identity, and its open restriction is a map between zero objects. It is therefore invertible by joint detection. Construct the open projection map j_!(j^*Q tensor P) -> Q tensor j_!P as the other mate. Its open restriction is invertible by the unit triangle identity. Disjointness in the closed restriction follows from the two adjunctions and the already-known opposite disjointness; tensor preserves zero objects because it is a left adjoint. Joint detection proves this second map invertible. For an arbitrary open immersion, realize its complement as the closed subscheme defined by the vanishing ideal of the closed complement. All constructions are natural transformations, and this argument proves their components invertible.

Compose the two natural projection isomorphisms for i and j. Use the canonical constant-module pullback compositor and its derived comparison to replace i^*j^* by (ji)^*. The existing ambient closed adjunction composed with the exact open adjunction gives Rs_! left adjoint to Rs^! with exactly the functors in the statement.

Upgrade each closed tensor-Hom adjunction to a parametrized adjunction using evaluation naturality. Apply the existing parametrized conjugate-isomorphism construction to the composite projection formula and the two adjunctions s^* left adjoint to Rs_* and Rs_! left adjoint to Rs^!. Uncurrying gives the required bifunctor isomorphism. The product naturality equation supplies contravariant naturality in P and covariant naturality in M. This is the blueprint Hom calculation and Yoneda argument, without any boundedness or constructibility restriction.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a locally closed immersion. On either
of the two finite-coefficient sites, and on the ambient derived
categories, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M)
\cong Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M).
$$

proof.text:
Factor $s$ into an open and a closed immersion. The adjunctions of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], [lem-exc-closed-ambient] construct
$Rs^!$ as their composite. Extension by zero for an open or closed
immersion is exact, and its stalkwise description gives, for all
complexes, $Q\otimes^LRs_!P=Rs_!(s^*Q\otimes^LP)$; use flat
resolutions to derive the tensor product. For every test complex
$Q$ on $X$, the adjunctions and the internal Hom of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M))
&=\operatorname{Hom}_X(Rs_!(s^*Q\otimes^LP),M)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_S(s^*Q\otimes^LP,Rs^!M)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M)).
\end{aligned}
$$

Yoneda proves the assertion. The maps are defined by evaluation and
the adjunction counits, so the identity is compatible with both.
